- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates prices; increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after a spike; add 2–5% to forecast for that window.
- Model overestimates prices in the 20–30 day horizon after a spike; reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model shows strong upward trend, adjust downward by 1–3% in the final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.73 to -0.53), reduce forecast by 3–5% in the next 5 days to reflect sentiment shift.
